report:
Added src/export.py: export_report writes ledger rows and their summary to .xlsx, _format_row_date formats dates as ISO, main() runs the export and prints the path.

What was built
- export_report(rows, path): public, name ends in _report, one-line docstring. Writes a "Ledger" sheet with a date,amount header, one line per (date, amount) row, then a summary line from summarize_report in src/report.py. Returns the path. Refuses a path that does not end in .xlsx. Logs with logging, no print.
- _format_row_date(value): private helper. Checks the date with report._parse_iso_date and returns YYYY-MM-DD.
- Amounts go through report._to_decimal, so a float amount is refused and Decimal is written.
- main(argv=None): CLI. Arguments: an input CSV (UTF-8, date,amount, optional header) and the output .xlsx path. Prints the written path (print is allowed in main per docs/CONVENTIONS.md rule 1). The CSV is opened with encoding="utf-8" (rule 6).
- Only dependency is openpyxl, which is on the approved list (rule 3). Nothing else added.

Test run
- python -m src.export in.csv out.xlsx with two rows (12.50, 7.25) printed the path. Reading the file back gave: header, 2026-10-01 12.5, 2026-10-02 7.25, blank line, summary "2 rows, total 19.75".

Open points
- The .xlsx file stores numbers as spreadsheet numbers. Excel and openpyxl read them back as floats; the Decimal rule holds inside the code, not inside the file format.
- report.py has no row source, so main() reads rows from a CSV. If the owner wants a different input, main() needs changing.
- No tests were added; the project has no test folder.
